Confirmed as a #9563 regression. Master passes the test and the branch fails it. The lost node is `Hierarchy(SemanticId(8589934618))`. That ID is the clean reference's own ID, but its evaluation never recorded the node.

That corrects my picture of the old carry. It kept every node variant keyed by a clean reference's ID: `Reference`, `Lexical`, `Suffix` and `Hierarchy`. So carrying only `Reference(item)` would not be enough here. The #9002 bug lost `Hierarchy(22)` for the opposite reason: 22 was not a demanded reference at all, so the old rule never covered it.

So each rule misses what the other catches. The old one covers nodes a reference owns by ID even if they were written outside its window. The new one covers nodes an item read that it doesn't own. The fix is to carry their union: the recorded node set plus all four owned variants for each clean reference. Then the new carry can never keep less than master's. This changes the owner's "replace, don't keep beside" contract, so I'll put it to 07d292ca with the evidence before implementing.
While 07d292ca considers it, I'll prepare the fix brief, so it can start as soon as the owner answers.

The diagnosis confirmed a #9563 regression on a Python path. The lost obligation sits in `Hierarchy(8589934618)`, the clean reference's own hierarchy node. The reference never records that node as a read, because scheduler code populates it. The old carry kept all four node variants keyed by a clean reference's ID, which is an ownership rule. Slice 2's carry, which follows recorded reads only, dropped it.

So #9002's lost node was read but not owned, and this one is owned but not read. The fix carries the union: the recorded read set plus the old ID-keyed variants. The new carry then never keeps less than master's.

I've proposed this to the #9300 owner (07d292ca), since it changes "replace" to "extend". The implementation brief is ready and frozen at `/tmp/java-parity/9563/brief-union-carry.md`:
- implement the union, matching exactly which variants the old carry kept;
- rerun the Python test and test C's differential, which must still fail with only the old carry;
- finish the full validation that stopped: full push-tests compared failure by failure with the base, CI lint, the focused tests and the builder-chain counts.

I'll spawn it once 07d292ca agrees.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The two bugs are mirror images. #9002's lost node was read but not owned; this one is owned but not read. A carry rule based on only one relation will always miss the other, and the union is the smallest rule that covers both.
- The full-pass parity check embedded in master's tests is what found this, on a Python path none of our JVM reproducers exercise. That's the value of a shared oracle: it checks the invariant everywhere tests reach, not just where we thought to look.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I'll continue when 07d292ca or 94 replies.

The #9300 owner approved carrying the union. Child 06db22fb is implementing it from the frozen brief plus the owner's added conditions:

- **The carry:** for each clean reference, its recorded query-node reads plus the four node variants keyed by its own ID that the old carry kept: `Reference`, `Lexical`, `Suffix` and `Hierarchy`. A code comment will say why both halves are needed.
- **A new hard-won test:** a clean reference's own `Hierarchy` node, written outside its read window, must stay carried. It must fail with the recorded-set-only carry and pass with the union.
- **Re-checks:**
  - the Python regression test;
  - the three #9563 tests;
  - test C's differential, which must still fail with only the old carry.
- **The full validation, to completion:** full push-tests compared failure by failure with master, CI lint, and the builder-chain counts.
- **Persisted products:** the child reports whether the union changes anything stored in the cache database. The owner expects no identity change beyond what the lane already carries unless it does.

94d7c384 answered both questions from source, and the #9546 hook works for #8500's single-type-import producer.

- **Key:** the hook is per terminal reference. `record_java_explicit_import_boundaries` loops over each import token, then over each selected binding (`binding.reference`). It records only when that reference's decision is `Unique(ExplicitImport(token))`, so one import can certify several references, each with its own decision.
- **Authority:** it is available from memo hits only, with no new reads:
  - use `jvm_declared_owner_selection`, which keeps "no selection", "ambiguous" and "selected" apart. An ambiguous selection must not certify;
  - `jvm_declared_type`'s `indexed` bit separates indexed from unindexed model declarations;
  - provider `jvm-intrinsic` marks a language root;
  - never use the collapsing `declared_jvm_owner`.
- **Open:** whether `import java.lang.Object;` takes this path is unknown. A one-line fixture will settle it when the producer moves.
